scope: Bounded public GitHub source and known public X-post research. Existing source inventory was inspected first. Ten high-value source contracts were retained; discovery search counts are not claims of exhaustive ecosystem or social coverage.

baseline.note: Counts are the current inventory, not newly trained capability or distinct documents. Existing customer/workflow/game/browser/drone/citation/entity/amount/email/phone/context/sponsor/silent-failure/IR/mailroom controls are not recounted as new. No rows were added by this research.

search.coverage_limit: Sorted-by-update discovery is a bounded sample. Secondary indexes were used only to locate primary source posts. No authenticated X search or Xiaohongshu claim is made in this report.

priority_findings.novelty: New external retrieval and answerability-gating benchmark, adjacent to existing IR controls and separate TREC; not a new prepared source yet.
priority_findings.observed_contract: Branch J is Codiv openjev-0.1, one batch Noul request per query with one relevance question per passage. Branch T is hosted TypeSafe Jev; NVIDIA is a separate cross-encoder. All rerankers use the same frozen top-20 hybrid candidates; sorting preserves the original hybrid rank on score ties. README describes XQuAD-EN (1,190 queries) and SciFact (300), with retrieval nDCG@10/Recall/MRR, calibration, and a separately frozen-context answer-generation stage.

priority_findings.proposed_comparison: Add explicitly named Open-Jev-2B and Open-Jev-9B branches to the same frozen candidate sets, plus Jev and strict-output GPT; keep raw APIs/timings and all failures. Report reranking, answerability gate, and downstream answer quality separately.

priority_findings.novelty: New racing and between-lap adaptation task; current drone snapshots and simple games do not establish this stateful control capability.
priority_findings.observed_contract: server.py maps structured telemetry to racing descriptions and asks two five-way Choices (racing line and pedals) plus a trouble Noul in one driving request. A separate end-of-lap request supplies one faster/same/slower Choice per corner. JavaScript supplies continuous steering/physics and records lap completion; the model selects discrete targets, not every low-level physics step.

priority_findings.proposed_comparison: Use identical seeded tracks, physics and initial conditions for every provider. Compare full-race completion, off-track/crash counts, valid laps, lap-time trajectory and end-to-end action age. Add fixed-policy and no-debrief ablations to isolate model choice from controller assistance.
priority_findings.training_proposal: If approved later, create original tracks/telemetry and race-engineer cases with explicit simulator-derived outcomes; split entire tracks and races, including all lap revisions, together. Do not convert only successful demo laps into a general success claim.

priority_findings.observed_contract: buildQuestions emits one Noul per hand-card/pile candidate, one best-move Choice including pass, and a pressure Score. An independent rules function computes legality. Execution can use either a validator prefilter or foul penalties; these modes materially change the controller.
critical_measurement_limits: No key or forceMock=true routes to synthetic mockAnswer and returns mock:true. A successful HTTP response alone does not prove model inference.
In no-foul mode, the independent legality oracle filters actions; report raw model false positives/negatives separately from execution validity and wins.
Missing Noul fields currently fall back to zero in the demo evaluator; benchmark collectors should retain missing/invalid outputs as failures instead.

direct_x_posts.author: edwartnoyola
direct_x_posts.text:
I built a racing game where Jev is the driver with Claude Code!

Jev picks the racing line and when to brake, given the speed and the corner ahead.

Jev has no memory, so after each lap the game hands it the times for all 11 corners and it decides where to push harder.
direct_x_posts.interpretation: Direct author description corroborates racing/debrief contract. Video was not downloaded or analyzed; lap success/quality not independently verified.

comparison_rules: Distinguish exact model repository, checkpoint revision, API resolved model, provider, precision, and calibration; similarly named OpenJev projects are not interchangeable.

Use the same visible inputs and finite candidate meanings for all providers. Compare compact strict-output GPT decisions separately from a full-distribution output contract; do not invent GPT probabilities.

Measure matched client timing boundaries, concurrency, warm/cold cache conditions, request retries/failures, and complete wall time. Source APIs and local H100 execution have different hardware/network boundaries.

For closed loops, pair seeds/environment/controller/clock limits and report full goal completion alongside raw model decision quality. Rule filtering, mock outputs and fallback actions must be attributed explicitly.
API list-price estimates, trial credits, local hardware rentals, and claimed deployment-normalized latency must be labelled separately from measured/billed cost.

Keep all external benchmark inputs/labels and observed errors out of later training. Generate new original controls from task contracts, with whole document/trace/track/template groups held together and unseen families for OOD.
A finite schema, a runnable demo, an author's post, a software fixture and a measured model benchmark are different evidence levels; this report claims source inspection only.
next_steps: Retain training pause. Decide which external holdouts to add, freeze contracts and license checks before any model run.
Prioritize RAG with our explicitly identified checkpoint branches, original racing/card simulators with complete-game metrics, and independently labelled judge tasks.
Use new task families for original future data design; do not increment 408,884 rows or 25 sources until generated data passes independent label/split/provenance audits.
